newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS LIFTED BY MEMORY OF HIS LATE COACH.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS LIFTED BY MEMORY OF HIS LATE COACH.

text.p: Tom Gullikson thinks his late brother Tim gave Pete Sampras the inspiration the defending champion needed to carry him through the final points of his torturous fifth-set tiebreak victory on Thursday at the U.S. Open.
"Maybe Timmy whispered to him and told him to hit it," Gullikson said of the way a sick and exhausted Sampras found the will to hit a second-serve ace at 7-7 in the tiebreaker.

A point later, Spaniard Alex Corretja double faulted and the top-seeded Sampras, who later needed two litres of intravenous fluid for his dehydrated condition, had somehow survived 7-6 5-7 5-7 6-4 7-6 and advanced to the semifinals.

Gullikson's twin brother Tim started coaching Sampras in 1992 and a year later the American was the world's number one player. Tim Gullikson was stricken with brain cancer a year ago January and died this spring.
"This one is for Tim, this one is for Tim," girlfriend Delaina Mulcahy said Sampras told her after the four-hour, nine- minute match -- the longest at the Open this year.
Gullikson said the performance by Sampras, who was bent over in pain after every point of the tiebreaker and struggled at times to stay on his feet, was an inspiration for all.

"This guy is number one in the world, he's got more money then he could ever spend, and here he's on the tennis court, getting sick on the court and he can still somehow manage to find the will to win the match," said Gullikson.
"Every step looked like his last. Literally every time he took a step you really wondered how he was going to take another step. It was amazing that he hit the shots that he did in the tiebreaker."
Gullikson had a sense that his brother was an influence.
"I think he thinks about Tim a lot and the lessons that Tim taught him," said Gullikson, who has coached Sampras as captain of the U.S. Davis Cup team the past three years.
Lessons such as, "Just fight to the end. Never say die. Find a way to win, even when you are not playing well or, in this case, not feeling well. Look for ways to win," said Gullikson.
"I'm sure that there will be a small part of Tim with Pete all the time. Pete can use that to help motivate himself at important times. He knows Tim is always with him."
